name: DRVTHRU
label: Drive-thru window
question: Does this building have any drive-thru windows?
rationale: A drive-thru window is a physical service space/feature; it also signals a secondary activity.

name: COURT
label: Food court
question: Is there a food court in this mall?
rationale: Presence of a specific space (food court) in the mall; also implies a food-service secondary activity.

name: FACIL
label: On a multibuilding complex
question: Is this building part of a multibuilding campus or complex? A campus or complex is a group of two or more buildings on the same site that are owned or operated by a single organization or individual.
rationale: Campus/complex membership is not ownership, tenure or use; no concept in the vocabulary covers it.

name: FACACT
label: Type of complex
question: What is the primary business or function of this group of buildings as a whole?
codes: 1=College, university, or junior college; 2=Primary or secondary school [grades K-12]; 3=Other type of school; 4=Office complex; 5=Retail complex; 6=Storage or distribution complex; 7=Religious campus or complex; 8=Hospital or other health care complex; 9=Lodging or resort complex; 10=Post office complex; 11=Prison or correctional facility; 12=Other type of government complex; ...
A_comment: use type of the complex, not the building
rationale: A principal-activity classification, stated at complex level; not an additional activity of the building.

name: LODOCCP
label: Lodging room percent occupancy
question: In 2018, on average, what percentage of the guest or occupant rooms in this building were occupied per night?
rationale: Average nightly share of guest rooms occupied measures how heavily the building is occupied.

name: WATR
label: Energy used for water heating
question: Was any energy used for heating water for purposes such as washing hands, dishes, or clothes?
rationale: Indicates whether energy is used for the water-heating end use; the water-heating alternative is allowed by rule.

name: COOK
label: Energy used for cooking
question: Was any energy used for cooking?
rationale: Indicates whether energy is used for the cooking end use, which also implies cooking equipment.

name: FASTFD
label: Fast food or small restaurant
question:
In addition to the food court that was mentioned earlier, which of these types of food preparation or serving areas are found in this building? Fast food or small restaurant?
(Smaller than ~3,000 square feet; includes area for food preparation and customer seating)
rationale: Asks which food preparation/serving areas exist; also implies a food-service secondary activity.

name: CAF
label: Cafeteria or large restaurant
question:
In addition to the food court that was mentioned earlier, which of these types of food preparation or serving areas are found in this building? Cafeteria or large restaurant?
(Larger than ~3,000 square feet; includes area for food preparation and customer seating)
rationale: Asks which food preparation/serving areas exist; also implies a food-service secondary activity.

name: HWTRM
label: Large amounts of hot water
question: Is any space in this building used for any activities requiring large amounts of hot water, such as a commercial dishwasher, laundry room, heated pool, steam room, whirlpool, or showers?
rationale: Asks whether any space hosts hot-water-intensive activities; it describes hot-water demand, not equipment.

name: FUELTUB
label: Fuel used for heating hot tub
codes: 5=Electricity; 1=Natural gas from underground pipes; 2=Propane (bottled gas); 3=Fuel oil; 99=Other; -2=Not applicable
rationale: Names the fuel used for an end use (hot tub heating); the fuel of the equipment fits equally.

name: COOKTOPFUEL
label: Fuel used by separate cooktop
codes: 5=Electricity; 1=Natural gas from underground pipes; 2=Propane (bottled gas); -2=Not applicable
rationale: Names the fuel used for cooking by the cooktop; the fuel of the equipment fits equally.

name: OVENFUEL
label: Fuel used by wall oven
codes: 5=Electricity; 1=Natural gas from underground pipes; 2=Propane (bottled gas); -2=Not applicable
rationale: Names the fuel used for cooking by the wall oven; the fuel of the equipment fits equally.

name: CROCKPOT
label: Crock-Pot or slow cooker used at least once per week
rationale: Weekly-use frequency of an appliance is usage behavior; it also implies the appliance is present.

name: RICECOOK
label: Rice cooker used at least once per week
rationale: Weekly-use frequency of an appliance is usage behavior; it also implies the appliance is present.

name: APPOTHER
label: Any other small kitchen appliance used at least once per week
rationale: Weekly-use frequency of an appliance is usage behavior; it also implies the appliance is present.

name: INTERNET
label: Internet access at home
codes: 1=Yes, by paying a cell phone company or Internet service provider; 2=Yes, without paying a cell phone company or Internet service provider; 0=No access to the Internet
rationale: Household internet access is not an energy or building concept; at most it is a loose household attribute.

name: INTYPEBROAD
label: Have Internet access using broadband service
rationale: Broadband service type is not an energy or building concept; at most it is a loose household attribute.

name: SSTV
label: Use smart speakers to control TV or peripherals
rationale: Presence/use of smart speakers to control home electronics; it describes devices more than energy management.

name: NGPAY
label: Who pays for natural gas
codes: 1=Household is responsible for paying for all natural gas used in this home; 2=All natural gas used in this home is included in the rent or condo fee; 3=Some is paid by the household, some is included in the rent or condo fee; 99=Other; -2=Do not use natural gas
rationale: Whether gas is paid by the household or included in rent is a tenure/lease arrangement, not an amount spent.

name: FOPAY
label: Who pays for fuel oil
codes: 1=Household is responsible for paying for all fuel oil used in this home; 2=All fuel oil used in this home is included in the rent or condo fee; 3=Some is paid by the household, some is included in the rent or condo fee; 99=Other; -2=Do not use fuel oil
rationale: Whether fuel oil is paid by the household or included in rent is a tenure/lease arrangement, not an amount spent.

name: SMARTMETER
label: Home has an electricity smart meter
rationale: Presence of smart metering infrastructure (enabling feedback and demand response), not the interval data itself.

name: INTDATAACC
label: Household member has viewed smart meter interval data
rationale: Use of smart-meter interval data as energy feedback is an energy-management practice, not the data itself.

name: SQFTRANGE
label: Respondent-reported square footage range
codes: 1=Less than 600 square feet; 2=600 to 799 square feet; 3=800 to 999 square feet; 4=1,000 to 1,499 square feet; 5=1,500 to 1,999 square feet; 6=2,000 to 2,499 square feet; 7=2,500 to 2,999 square feet; 8=3,000 square feet or more
rationale: A binned square-footage range is exactly the floor area category concept.
